chunks: And likewise, what Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام used to say:

There is no بأس in the leftover of a mouse when it has drunk from a vessel: that one may drink from it and perform wudu (ablution) from it. The reason in this is that it is specified, apart from those whose flesh is not eaten, because it is not possible to guard oneself from the mouse and that is burdensome upon the human being; so its leftover was excused on account of that.

key_terms.سُؤْرِ: the leftover drink or remainder in a vessel after an animal has drunk from it
key_terms.فَعُفِيَ: it was excused or overlooked in the legal ruling
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأَ: to perform wudu (ablution) using that water
key_terms.ٱلتَّحَرُّزُ: avoiding or guarding oneself against something
key_terms.ٱلْإِنَاءِ: the vessel or container from which the mouse drank
key_terms.ٱلْفَأْرَةِ: the mouse, whose leftover is specifically discussed here

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to drink from or perform wudu (ablution) with water from which a mouse has drunk?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the leftover water of a mouse in a vessel is excused, so drinking from it and using it for wudu (ablution) is permitted. It explains the basis of the ruling as hardship and the difficulty of avoiding mice, distinguishing this case from other animals whose flesh is not eaten.
